note: Audit 534494-c1/534494-s1: Same article, same medium and same variable. The claim (SI p.2) states that changing the fluence modifies the particle size in deionized water; series 534494-s1 is the article's water experiment at 800 nm, 30 fs, 1 kHz, TEM geometric-diameter particle-count mean, with two fluence points (0.25 and 1 J/cm2) that correspond to the two water syntheses the text reports (SI p.2: 6 nm at ~0.25 J/cm2, 434 particles; main p.2-3: 26 nm at ~1 J/cm2, 324 particles). No variable, material, wavelength or statistic proxy is needed, so the pair is comparable on the stated terms.; caveats: Two points only, so the shape is just the sign of the slope and no interior structure is tested. The claim also asserts a change of the size distribution, while the series carries only the mean size, so that half of the sentence is untested. The ~0.25 J/cm2 point was produced with a neutral density filter replacing the GO absorption (main p.5 and Methods p.7: "we replaced the absorption contribution of H2O + GO by a neutral optical density filter ... achieving this way a fluence of ~0.25 J/cm2 in the target"), so it is a water experiment at reduced fluence, not a second GO experiment; the SI section 1 heading nevertheless reads "Particles created in GO + H2O using a fluence of ~0.25 J/cm2", while its Fig. S1 caption and the main text place that synthesis in H2O only. Point errors are the stored SD over sqrt(N) (SD 2.4 nm, N=434; SD 12.4 nm, N=324), not the 10%/20% fallback, so the two-point shape is insensitive to the error model.
